# Audit Dataset

**Source execution:** Read `$NUREC_WORKDIR/nurec-runtime.md`, generated by
`run.sh`, before executing commands. For every root-workspace `bazel` command
below, use its literal Docker/Bazel prefix with the same target and arguments.
Only the standalone converter workspace runs Bazel on the host. Do not extract
release archives into host caches or invent module overrides.

This step audits a raw sensor dataset and generates an input YAML for
`nurec-onboard`. It is usually run standalone before the full workflow:

```bash
./run.sh /path/to/audit.yaml --agent <claude|codex> --step audit-dataset
./run.sh "$NUREC_WORKDIR/audit-<data.name>/<data.name>_input.yaml" --agent <claude|codex>
```

This step is read-only with respect to `data.path`. It does not scaffold a
converter, run conversion, validate an NCore shard, or launch NuRec.

---

## 1. Input Schema

```yaml
data:
  name: <string> # Filesystem-safe dataset identifier.
  path: <string> # Path to one raw sequence or sequence root.
  docs: <string> | [<string>, ...] # Optional citable dataset docs: URL, file path, inline text, QA doc, paper, datasheet, or data-owner answer.
  hints: <string> # Optional operator-known facts to verify.

audit_output_dir: <string> # Optional; default: $NUREC_WORKDIR/audit-<data.name>
```

`data.description` is not required on audit input. The audit's job is to produce
a short high-level `data.description` and a structured `data.profile` in the
generated workflow input.

---

## 2. Minimum Dataset Facts

Before choosing the output structure, derive the minimum useful dataset facts
from public NCore and NuRec interfaces, plus the existing converter
critical-parameter contract. The generated YAML should contain facts under
`data.profile` whenever they are observable or documented; otherwise it should
mark the item with an `UNRESOLVED:` description and explain the YAML path in
the report.

### NCore-facing facts

- Input inventory: camera, LiDAR, radar, pose, mask, and cuboid raw inputs;
  canonical sensor IDs; included/excluded decisions.
- File layout: paths relative to `data.path`, file formats, field names, units,
  and dtypes.
- Frame conventions: rig, world, camera, LiDAR, and cuboid frames; transform
  directions exposed by calibration files.
- Camera calibration: model family, resolution, distortion state, intrinsics,
  shutter type, and per-frame timestamp semantics.
- LiDAR calibration: spinning/solid-state type, beam model, row/column counts,
  per-beam elevations, per-column azimuths, per-row azimuth offsets, intensity
  scale, and per-ray timestamp availability.
- Pose trajectory: raw pose inputs, timestamp coverage, transform direction,
  and whether a global/ECEF/UTM frame is present.
- Sequence interval: timestamp units and modality coverage needed to choose a
  valid conversion envelope.
- Masks and cuboids: mask names/polarity, cuboid centroid convention,
  `dimensions` as a `{length, width, height}` source-field mapping, yaw
  convention, class labels, and label source.

### NuRec-facing facts

- `nurec.camera_ids` and exactly one entry in `nurec.lidar_ids` when the
  operator wants a scoped NuRec run. Keep `lidar_ids` as a list so the input
  shape can expand when NuRec supports multi-LiDAR training.
- Per-camera ego masks keyed as `ego` when available, with positive polarity.
- Camera timing and shutter facts needed for rolling-shutter compensation.
- LiDAR timestamp quality and model facts needed for motion compensation.
- Cuboid conventions and coverage for dynamic-scene reconstruction.
- Known limitations that affect reconstruction quality, such as missing ego
  masks, absent cuboids, unsupported sensors, or incomplete pose coverage.

### Critical-parameter bridge

Translate the converter's required critical parameters into descriptive input
facts. For example, the audit may say where beam elevations live, what the
camera frame convention is, or which timestamp field is sweep end; it must not
prescribe converter function names or composition recipes.

### High-risk facts

Some descriptive facts are high-impact and silently wrong when guessed. For
each field below, cite a matching `data.docs` entry when documentation answers
it; otherwise write `UNRESOLVED:` at the generated YAML path and explain the
gap in the report. Do not promote heuristics such as FOV, raw field names, or a
single matrix inspection into confirmed facts.

- `data.profile.cameras[].model_family`
- `data.profile.cameras[].distortion_model`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.static_transforms[].direction`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.rig_frame`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.camera_frame`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.lidar_frame`
- `data.profile.cuboids.reference_frame`
- `data.profile.cuboids.centroid`
- `data.profile.lidars[].motion_compensation`
- `data.profile.lidars[].spinning.direction`

Documentation is an opportunistic evidence source, not a precondition for
running audit-dataset. When no documentation answers a high-risk fact, leaving
that field unresolved is the intended behavior.

The validator enforces only the structural half of this rule: each high-risk
field must be concrete or an `UNRESOLVED:` marker. The supporting `data.docs`
citation for a concrete value is the author's responsibility and is not
machine-checked.

#### Blocking vs converter-derivable

The list above governs _shape_: every one of those fields must be concrete or
carry an `UNRESOLVED:` marker, never blank or null. Severity is a separate
question. A marker blocks unless a deterministic procedure over the raw data
settles the fact, in which case it is advisory: record it in
`advisory_unresolved` and continue.

**Always blocking.** Conventions the raw data cannot settle -- an extrinsic
matrix is equally valid read in either direction, so no inspection of it
recovers which direction was intended, and the same holds for axis conventions
and distortion-coefficient ordering. An unresolved marker here always stops the
workflow before `build-ncore-converter`. Do not reclassify them:

- `data.profile.cameras[].model_family`
- `data.profile.cameras[].distortion_model`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.static_transforms[].direction`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.rig_frame`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.camera_frame`
- `data.profile.calibration_and_frames.lidar_frame`

**Potentially converter-derivable.** The remaining high-risk fields, where a
measurement may exist: sweep direction from azimuth ordering, motion
compensation from points against the ego trajectory, cuboid centroid and
reference frame by projection against LiDAR returns.

To claim derivable, the marker must name the raw artifact, the procedure, and
the procedure's precondition, as in `"UNRESOLVED: Derive spinning direction
from the range-image azimuth ordering before conversion."` A marker that only
restates the question stays blocking, and so does one whose precondition this
input fails -- a stationary clip cannot resolve motion compensation against the
ego trajectory.

Classify by this distinction when reporting `blocking_unresolved_count`.

---

## 3. Instructions

> **Step attempt entry anchor:** capture `runs[*].started_at` here, before the
> "Parse input" actions below; see
> [nurec-onboard/SKILL.md "Timestamp capture rules"](../../SKILL.md#timestamp-capture-rules)
> for the step-attempt definition.

### Parse input

1. Extract `data.name`, `data.path`, optional `data.docs`, optional `data.hints`,
   and optional `audit_output_dir`.
2. Derive `audit_output_dir` when absent: `$NUREC_WORKDIR/audit-<data.name>`.
3. Verify `data.path` exists and is a non-empty directory.
4. Record the input docs/hints in the report as operator-provided starting
   evidence, not as conclusions.

### Read docs and hints

1. Treat each `data.docs` item as a distinct evidence source and preserve its
   original URL, file path, directory path, or inline label in the report.
   Redact credentials from a URL before writing it anywhere in the report: drop
   any `user:password@` userinfo and replace the value of a credential-bearing
   query parameter such as `token`, `key`, `sig`, or `signature` with
   `REDACTED`. Keep the rest of the URL so the citation still identifies the
   source.
2. Read file-path docs directly. For a directory, inspect its index or README
   first, then enumerate the tree and prioritize files relevant to dataset
   structure, calibration, sensors, timestamps, and annotations. Do not read a
   large tree exhaustively: record each file read and summarize skipped groups
   with their paths and the reason they were not needed.
3. If `data.docs` points to an authenticated
   private URL that WebFetch cannot load, record that fetch failure in
   `## Documentation Coverage` and leave any dependent high-risk facts
   unresolved unless the input also provides a local file, inline note, paper,
   datasheet, or data-owner answer that resolves them.
4. Fetch URL docs only when the launcher allowlist permits the host. The
   launcher derives that allowlist from `data.docs` URL hostnames. WebFetch does
   not authenticate to private repos, and URLs expose path/query strings to the
   target server, so do not put secrets in documentation URLs.
5. Use inline text, QA notes, datasheets, papers, and data-owner answers as
   provided, but cite them separately from fetched URLs or local files.
6. In the report's `## Documentation Coverage` section, record the actual outcome
   for every source and every file selected from a directory: loaded OK, skipped
   as irrelevant, blocked by allowlist, HTTP error, render/parse failure, missing
   path, or inline source consumed. Do not silently skip a docs item.
7. When a provided URL fails to fetch or render, an authoritative alternate
   source may resolve the same fact (for example a dataset paper, datasheet, or
   data-owner answer). Record both the failed primary source and the alternate
   source that resolved the fact.
8. Treat `data.hints` as hypotheses to verify against docs or raw data.

### Walk the raw data

Enumerate every top-level raw input and recurse where needed to classify:

- camera, LiDAR, radar, pose, calibration, mask, cuboid, metadata, or other.
- file count, extensions, sample file shape/keys/header, and timestamp-looking fields.
- include/exclude/ambiguous decision with a reason.

Resolve obvious aliases to canonical sensor IDs, but do not invent missing IDs.

### Probe sensor-suite facts

Use lightweight filesystem and format probes. System Python is permitted here
because the audit does not import NCore. If a dataset SDK is available in the
current environment, it may be used to decode the dataset's own metadata.

Probe at least:

- Camera resolutions, intrinsics fields, distortion coefficient order, image
  format, shutter direction, shutter duration, and timestamp meaning.
- LiDAR point/range-image fields, beam metadata, azimuth/timestamp/intensity
  raw inputs, motion-compensation state, sweep duration, and timestamp meaning.
- Calibration extrinsics and transform direction for every sensor.
- Pose raw inputs, pose timestamp units, pose source density, and frame origin.
- Cuboid example records, centroid convention, dimension axis order, yaw zero,
  class vocabulary, and duplicate/sensor-specific label indicators.
- Mask files, names, encoding domain, and polarity.

### Emit the generated input YAML

Write `<audit_output_dir>/<data.name>_input.yaml` using the skeleton structure in
`nurec-onboard/steps/audit-dataset/input-skeleton.yaml`:

```yaml
data:
  name: <data.name>
  path: <data.path>
  description: >
    <short high-level overview of the dataset, with no facts duplicated from
    data.profile>
  profile:
    file_layout: { ... }
    calibration_and_frames: { ... }
    pose_sources: [...]
    timestamp_semantics: { ... }
    cameras: [...]
    lidars: [...]
    cuboids: { ... }
    known_gaps: [...]
  docs:
    - <preserved docs entries, if any>
ncore:
  camera_ids: [...]
  lidar_ids: [...]
  seek_sec: <number|null>
  duration_sec: <number|null>
  converter_dir: <string|null>
  output_dir: <string|null>
nurec:
  camera_ids: [...]
  lidar_ids: [...] # Exactly one converted LiDAR ID; NuRec trains on a single LiDAR per run.
  output_dir: <string|null>
  dev_deps_image: <string|null> # Optional; defaults to the checkout's build-image pin.
  source_dir: <string|null> # Optional; defaults to the enclosing checkout.
execution:
  max_inner_iterations: <int> # Optional override; default from defaults.yaml.
  max_outer_iterations: <int> # Optional override; default from defaults.yaml.
  max_config_iterations: <int> # Optional override; default from defaults.yaml.
```

Rules:

- `data.description` is a human-readable overview only. Do not duplicate
  structured facts there.
- Every concrete fact in `data.profile` must be backed by a doc citation, file
  path/key, or measured probe value. The "High-risk facts" section above sets
  the higher confirmation bar for the fields it lists.
- Unknown minimum facts or scope choices must appear as `UNRESOLVED:`
  descriptions in the relevant generated input field. The validator derives the
  unresolved key from the YAML path.
- Preserve the skeleton's field order and section spacing. Insert one blank line
  after `data.description`, between each major `data.profile` section, after
  `data.docs` when present, and between the top-level `ncore` and `nurec`
  blocks.
- Record-like list entries must be readable block-style mappings with one field
  per line. This applies to camera records, LiDAR records, pose sources, static
  and dynamic transforms, mask records, raw input records, and per-ray metadata.
  Short scalar lists may stay inline, such as `resolution: [1920, 1080]` and
  `distortion_coeff_order: [k1, k2, p1, p2, k3]`. Nested mappings, including
  `cuboids.dimensions`, should use one field per line.
- Do not include converter implementation instructions, function names,
  composition formulas, or references to private converters.

### Emit the data-quality report

Write `<audit_output_dir>/<data.name>_data_quality_report.md` with these
required sections:

```markdown
# Data Quality Report -- <data.name>

## Summary

## Documentation Coverage

## Minimum NCore/NuRec Facts

## Sensor Facts

## Confirmed Parameters

## Critical Gaps

## Warnings

## Operator Next Steps
```

The Critical Gaps section must mention the YAML path for every `UNRESOLVED:`
field in the generated input YAML and explain what is missing, why it matters,
and where the operator should look next.

### Emit the audit profile

Write `<audit_output_dir>/audit_profile.json` with a machine-readable summary
that mirrors `data.profile` and adds bridge fields for the later
converter-local `dataset_probe.py` checklist:

```json
{
  "nurec_onboard_version": "<NuRec Onboard release version>",
  "dataset": {"name": "...", "path": "..."},
  "profile": { "...": "same structured facts as data.profile" },
  "minimum_facts": {"confirmed": [...], "unresolved": [...]},
  "dataset_probe_hints": {
    "calibrations": [],
    "timestamps": [],
    "cuboids": [],
    "lidar_points": []
  }
}
```

Set `nurec_onboard_version` to the NuRec Onboard release identifier, the
`version` in the frontmatter of `nurec-onboard/SKILL.md`.

```bash
bazel run //skills/nurec-onboard/validators:audit_dataset_validator -- --print-nurec-onboard-version
```

The audit profile informs, but does not replace, the converter workdir's
`dataset_probe.py`. `build-ncore-converter` still owns that file and fills it
after the template is materialized.

### Validate outputs

Run the audit artifact validator before returning:

```bash
cd "$NUREC_ONBOARD_DIR" && bazel run //skills/nurec-onboard/validators:audit_dataset_validator -- \
  <audit_output_dir>/<data.name>_input.yaml \
  <audit_output_dir>/<data.name>_data_quality_report.md \
  <audit_output_dir>/audit_profile.json
```

If validation fails, fix the artifacts and re-run once. If it still fails,
return the diagnostics verbatim.

> **Step attempt exit anchor:** capture `runs[*].ended_at` here, after
> validation succeeds; see
> [nurec-onboard/SKILL.md "Timestamp capture rules"](../../SKILL.md#timestamp-capture-rules)
> for the step-attempt definition.

---

## 4. Output Contract

On success, return:

```yaml
status: success | partial
generated_input_yaml: <path>
data_quality_report: <path>
audit_profile: <path>
unresolved_count: <int> # every UNRESOLVED: entry, both severities
blocking_unresolved_count: <int> # the subset that blocks, per the rule below
advisory_unresolved: [<string>, ...] # YAML paths of the advisory remainder
notes: [<string>, ...]
```

Classify every `UNRESOLVED:` entry by
["Blocking vs converter-derivable"](#blocking-vs-converter-derivable) above: an
entry blocks unless a deterministic procedure over the raw data settles the
fact, so a high-risk field whose marker names that procedure and its
precondition counts as advisory. Only blocking entries stop the workflow; the
orchestrator gates on `blocking_unresolved_count`.

Use `partial` when `blocking_unresolved_count` is above zero. Advisory
entries alone still return `success`.

The Critical Gaps report section and `audit_profile.json`'s
`minimum_facts.unresolved` stay complete regardless: both list every
unresolved field, whichever severity. A reader needs the whole picture even
when only a subset stops the run.

---

## 5. Constraints

- Read-only on `data.path`.
- No converter scaffolding and no edits under `ncore.converter_dir`.
- No Docker or NuRec launch.
- No NCore imports under system Python.
- Descriptive dataset facts only; do not encode converter implementation
  instructions in `data.profile` or `data.description`.
